title: Asymptotes of a Linear-over-Linear Rational Function
originalTopic: Vertical and horizontal asymptotes from a graph
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x) = (x + 1)/(x - 1), determine the vertical and horizontal asymptotes, and explain what a graphing window such as [-6, 6] by [-6, 6] shows about the two branches.

steps.title: Find the vertical asymptote
steps.explanation: The denominator vanishes at x = 1 while the numerator equals 2 there, so the two one-sided limits blow up with opposite signs.
steps.why: A zero of the denominator that is not canceled by the numerator always produces a vertical asymptote.

steps.title: Rewrite to expose the horizontal asymptote
steps.explanation: Division shows the function as 1 plus a term that shrinks to zero, so y = 1 is the horizontal asymptote approached from below on the left and above on the right.
steps.why: Equating degrees in numerator and denominator gives a horizontal asymptote at the ratio of leading coefficients, here 1/1 = 1.

steps.title: Interpret the plotted picture
steps.explanation: The plot shows two hyperbola-like branches separated by the gap at x = 1, each flattening onto y = 1; because degrees match, there is no slant asymptote.
steps.why: Software often draws a near-vertical line at x = 1 that looks like part of the curve, so knowing the true asymptote prevents misreading it.
